dialogues.speaker: Sereda
dialogues.text: Well, between you and me, I found some damp rye and potatoes frozen hard as rocks. Only one-fifth the usual price.

dialogues.speaker: Sereda
dialogues.text: For a unit with a limited food budget, the most important things are "filling stomachs" and "not poisoning anyone."

dialogues.speaker: Sereda
dialogues.text: But a combat chef's duty is to take the cheapest, most ordinary ingredients and turn them into meals that satisfy the soldiers.

dialogues.speaker: Sereda
dialogues.text: So the staples I buy may not be the finest quality. The priority is quantity above all else.

dialogues.speaker: Sereda
dialogues.text: Whatever funds are left go toward ingredients that improve the flavor, like well-seasoned cured meat and rimecurrant.

dialogues.speaker: Sereda
dialogues.text: Lately, I've been trying to make a new kind of cured-meat bread. Ideally, it should be simple, tasty, and easy for soldiers stationed on the front lines to eat over long periods of time...
